title: The Inventory of the fourth floor walk-up
premise: After his mother's funeral, Mara Sterling returns to the fourth-floor walk-up where he grew up invisible beneath her silence, cataloging every object and everything she never said. When the building is scheduled for auction, Mara discovers a locked drawer of letters addressed to him—unsent for thirty years—revealing that her silence was not indifference but a deliberate erasure of his father's memory. As the auction date closes in, Mara must decide whether to preserve the apartment as a museum of avoidance or finally speak the goodbye neither of them managed. He ends by reading one letter aloud to the empty rooms before the new owners arrive, walking out with only the inventory itself.
about_author: Sebastian Delacroix is a former estate appraiser who spent a decade cataloging the belongings of strangers' dead. He writes quietly devastating fiction about the objects we leave behind and the words we don't.

chapters.title: The Fourth Floor Walk-Up
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Three days after the funeral, he moves back into the walk-up to prepare it for sale, beginning a meticulous written inventory of each room—and, alongside it, a parallel list of everything his mother never said. The emotional beat is numb grief sharpening into unease as he notices the apartment has been curated: certain drawers locked, certain years absent from the photographs.

chapters.title: What the Appraiser Overlooked
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. An auction house appraiser values the furniture but dismisses an old writing desk as worthless; alone that night, Mara pries open its locked drawer and finds decades of unsent letters addressed to him, all beginning 'My dear boy.' The emotional beat is vertigo—the inventory of silence was wrong, because she had been speaking all along, just never aloud.

chapters.title: Auction Day
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. On auction morning, relatives and strangers bid on his childhood while Mara reads the letters in the stairwell, learning his father didn't abandon them—he was erased, and Mara's own invisibility was the price of his mother's control. The climax arrives when the winning bidder knocks and Mara must choose between letting the rooms be sold silent or saying something first.

chapters.title: Out Loud
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Alone in the emptied apartment on the final evening, Mara reads the last unsent letter aloud to the bare walls—a proper goodbye, spoken at last into rooms that will never hold them again. He leaves behind the furniture but keeps his two inventories, now merged into one honest document. The emotional beat is release: grief transmuted into voice, and identity reclaimed.
